t.E354.agn: According to EFSA, animal studies showed no toxic effects, including effects on the kidney, and no genotoxic potential. In 2020 EFSA set a group ADI for E 334–337 and E 354 of 240 mg/kg body weight per day, expressed as tartaric acid (replacing the SCF's 1990 ADI of 30 mg/kg), and stated that estimated exposure did not exceed this limit in any age group.
t.E354.body: Absorption of L(+)-tartaric acid is lower in humans than in rats.
t.E354.found.1: Fine bakery wares such as cakes and biscuits
t.E354.prod: Obtained by precipitation from the reaction of potassium bitartrate in wine lees with calcium hydroxide and calcium sulphate.
t.E354.regx.0: Re-evaluated; group ADI for E 334–337 and E 354 of 240 mg/kg body weight per day (as tartaric acid); exposure does not exceed the ADI.
t.E354.regx.1: Removed from Group I by 2024/1451; permitted at maximum levels within the 'tartaric acid–tartrates' group; removed from the infant formulae category (13.1.3). Applies from 16.12.2024.
t.E354.summary: The calcium salt of tartaric acid. Used as an acidity regulator.
t.E354.what: The calcium salt of tartaric acid; it regulates the acidity of food.
